Target: Test whether OpenCode can execute as an Orca-supervised sub-agent in the existing Strata worktree. This is a user-requested integration smoke test, not a research or implementation task. Keep the OpenCode model and agent configuration exactly as launched; do not select a model or change settings.
Change: Read the files AGENTS.md and CMakeLists.txt in /home/yayoi/orca/workspaces/Strata/sycl using your actual tools. For each, compute the byte count and SHA256, and provide a brief one-sentence description based on reading the file. Write exactly one JSON report at /home/yayoi/orca/workspaces/Strata/sycl/bench/results/2026-10-15-pr6-recovery-audit/orca-opencode-default-smoke-worker-v1.json, with schema=1, marker="ORCA_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_SMOKE_20261017_V1", status="completed", files=[{path,bytes,sha256,description}], primary_branch, upstream, model_selection="unchanged_launch_default". Include no credentials or environment dumps. Maximum report size 4096 bytes.
Constraints: Read-only except that one named report. No product edits, Git commands, GPU jobs, builds, tests, profilers, process inspection, network research, new workers, or configuration changes. The user explicitly chose OpenCode with its default model for this smoke test; this supersedes normal Luna research-model rules only for this test.
Ownership: You own only the named report. Main owns all other files and resource cleanup. Finish within five minutes; if blocked, report the actual blocker through the injected orchestration protocol.
Observable acceptance: The coordinator can parse your JSON, independently match both byte counts and hashes, and verify your task/dispatch-specific worker_done through Orca. Follow the injected live orchestration preamble, check your inbox, and send worker_done exactly once with the actual report path and lifecycle IDs. Then idle. Return a short completion statement without starting further work.
